epic.intent:
Replace Bannerlord's human appearance system and creator with equivalent customization controls and visual quality to Dragon's Dogma 2, using a Bannerlord-fitting asset catalog. User confirmed all human characters including troops, and original catalog rather than copying DD2's complete selection catalog. D2 (2026-10-18) changes the asset rule for the development phase: development assets may derive from DD2, every asset's lineage is recorded, and every dd2-derived asset is replaced by a reference-only clean remake before any public or Workshop release (a future epic); the original catalog remains the release target. Cover player, nobles, companions, civilians, bandits, troops, all native male/female maturity definitions and adult aging. Improvements must appear in actual gameplay, equipment and portraits as well as the creator. The primary acceptance is the visual quality of the characters the game produces, ordinary NPCs and troops especially, plus the player (D1). This is a vetted future implementation plan, not implemented or runtime-verified functionality.

Study DD2's complete human creator controls and observable behavior, then build and validate Bannerlord-native or explicitly proven extended mechanisms. Keep full control/quality parity as the outcome; unsupported capabilities are unmet requirements, not permission to silently narrow the result. A narrowing or deferral that the user chooses in the capability-decision record (MMR-265) and saves as a success-criterion edit is explicit, not silent. Asset production is required work, including modeling, deformation, material/texture authoring, hair and necessary equipment corrections. In this epic it runs through the D2 route: an agent-run AI remake pipeline (AssetHelper, Blender, RE Mesh Editor, REtool texture conversion) working on locally extracted DD2 meshes, rigs and textures under supervised autonomy, with the user's visual verdicts at checkpoints as the quality gate. No assumption that an imported static model, one added slider, XML references, or code generation alone delivers the requested result.

Installed-file evidence establishes Bannerlord v1.4.8, shared human heads across ten skin definitions, 63 declared deform keys per skin, a 512-bit static appearance container, a 320-entry marshalled weight array and native FaceGen calls; none of these establishes extension capacity. DD2 and REFramework are installed, but complete creator mapping and fresh runtime/toolchain validation remain required. Scope and product decisions will be frozen before dependent production, with no unsupported feature marked complete. Execution is not requested now; save in Backlog and start no run.

## Races and peoples (added 2026-10-15)

User-confirmed extension: the overhaul and creator also set up the FWGC++ races, so every character of every people uses this system, not only humans. Every human-only requirement above now applies to every people. Per D10, troops and civilians use the system on their vanilla presentation culture's characters and race until the per-people content epic takes over troop and civilian race.

- **Races and peoples.** FWGC++ defines three parent races (human, elf, dwarf) and 12 peoples in `generator/data/heritage-appearance.json` (an authored body per race plus a per-people delta) at the `worldgen/producer.lock.json` commit. They map to five Bannerlord races (D14, 2026-10-18): human, elf, dwarf, gnome and tidekin. Gnome and tidekin are their own races, each with its own head and body meshes built from its FWGC++ race body and people delta; the tidekin race head carries the nictitating eyelid. The other ten peoples resolve to their race plus their authored delta (human_heartland, elf and dwarf are their races' bases; the five other human peoples and hill and frosthold dwarf are deltas). The people ids come from the people registry of the map epic (ep_01m513vch3mz0md6eqybvt1nmh, MMR-204), which owns the creator's people list and generation timing. This epic owns how each people looks and what it gains, and fills the registry's race and boon slots.
- **Default heights match the source.** Each people's creator default is its `frame.height_m` mean for the sex, and generated characters fall within its min–max. Build, mass and proportions (heads tall, shoulder, leg and hand ratios) follow the same data. Male means for example: human 1.74 m, elf 1.86 m, tidekin 1.76 m, dwarf 1.27 m, frosthold dwarf 1.29 m, hill dwarf 1.16 m, gnome 1.05 m at 4.2 heads tall. Uniform scaling is not assumed to be enough.
- **Pointy ears.** Elf `long_swept_point`, gnome `long_pointed_jug`, tidekin `finned_low_swept`; the other peoples keep rounded forms. Ear shape is editable in the creator and must work with hair, helmets and detail levels.
- **Fantasy skin colours.** One unrestricted skin colour palette, including non-natural hues, for every race. Each people's FWGC++ swatches are its default and population palette. D4 (2026-10-18) defines unrestricted: a free colour for the player and named heroes as a per-hero bake input, and an authored per-race palette of at least 24 swatches, non-natural hues included, for generated characters and troops.
- **Boons.** Each of the 12 peoples has its own boons in the style of the vanilla culture bonuses, shown on its creator selection and working in gameplay. The user approves the boon table before it is frozen.
- **Detailed Character Creation support.** The new creator must support Detailed Character Creation v1.8.1 (`zzCharacterCreation`, Workshop 2886299887) and its Additional Sliders add-on v1.8.0 (`zzCharacterCreation_AdditionalSliders`, Workshop 3072569986), both installed locally. Installed-file evidence: the add-on's `skins.xslt` adds 19 body deform keys to each of the ten skins of race `human` only, and DCC ships builds for game v1.3.4–v1.3.13 while the pinned game is v1.4.8. Whether DCC loads on the pinned build, and how its keys reach non-human races, must be proven. DCC stays an optional companion module, never a required dependency, and its files are never redistributed.

Unsupported race capabilities are unmet requirements, as above, not permission to narrow the result.

The primary acceptance is the visual quality of the characters it produces, NPCs and troops included (D1). Its organisation follows DD2's five tabs and the ledger's 196 families (474 controls; docs/character-overhaul/reference-controls.json, D17) wherever that is cheap; a one-to-one copy of DD2's UI is a nice-to-have, not an acceptance requirement. Provide the agreed grouping, selection previews, numerical precision, linked/independent behaviour, resets and undo/redo around real runtime state. Use transactional preview sessions and integrate commit/cancel with persistence (MMR-172). A diagnostic or temporarily unbound production resource may support development, but required controls cannot be hidden or replaced by placeholders in the completed integrated creator.

The creator replaces the FaceGen movie inside the vanilla BodyGeneratorView with CharacterCreatorVM over the same BodyGenerator and IFaceGeneratorHandler, organised in DD2's five tabs from the frozen ledger. One slider may drive one or two keys through DependencyResolver, with influence and clamp rules matched to the ledger's tables. Surface controls run a 512x512 live bake and a full bake on commit. DCC's 19 keys appear in the Body tab. The skin-colour control writes the free colour that D4 (c) gives the player and named heroes into the record as a bake input; MMR-223 owns the per-race palettes and people defaults. The race selector appears whenever FaceGen.GetRaceCount() > 1, which with MNBL.CharacterOverhaul.Races loaded means all five races: human, elf, dwarf, gnome and tidekin (D14, D16). The creator lives in the core module and works on vanilla Sandbox and StoryMode without the races module.
